newsitem.title: USA: Hein-Werner Q1 hurt by fluid power unit.
newsitem.headline: Hein-Werner Q1 hurt by fluid power unit.

text.p: Hein-Werner Corp attributed its lower first-quarter results to weak performance by its Great Bend Industries fluid power division and to high operational expenses related to the consolidation of certain collision repair operations in western Europe.
The company said shortly after the quarter ended, it agreed to sell Great Bend Industries and will use the approximately $22 million in proceeds to reduce debt and add new business segments.
It also signed a multi-year contract with John Bean Co under which Hein-Werner will manufacture brake lathes, stands and accessories.

Overall, Hein-Werner said it beleives its U.S. business is solid and president Joseph Dindorf in a statement said the company was confident its efforts to build shareholder value will result in "a solid year for 1997."
For the March 29 first quarter, the company reported earnings of $0.10 per share compared with $0.28 per share a year earlier. Sales declined to $16.1 million from $17.6 million.
